spec_architectural_decisions.decision: Fix is a SQL-side ::int cast on the COUNT(*)/SUM(integer) projection columns, NOT a C#-side switch from GetInt32 to GetInt64.
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: The repo's own hot-lessons documents '::int cast veya GetInt64' as the sanctioned remedy. ::int keeps the reader.GetInt32 calls, accumulator types, and DTO int fields byte-identical — minimal diff, behavior-preserving. Per-tenant COUNT/SUM values (leads, review_alerts, appointments-per-slot, wa_intents-per-analysis, return_deflections, daily_metrics sums) are orders of magnitude below int.MaxValue, so the narrowing cast never overflows in practice.
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: ::int on COUNT(*)/SUM(int) is the documented repo pattern, not a lossy hack. Decimal/numeric SUM columns (SUM(value_amount), SUM(deflection_revenue)) are read via GetDecimal and were deliberately NOT cast. CASE-division columns read via GetDouble were deliberately NOT cast.

spec_architectural_decisions.decision: Cross-service single commit (6 services) for one cohesive defect class (GetInt32-on-bigint), no Invekto.Shared change.
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: Each edit is an independent per-service repository SQL literal; they share no symbol. Bundling the same mechanical fix in one reviewable commit is clearer than 6 near-identical commits. No Shared/contract surface is touched, so there is no cross-service coupling introduced.
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: not a microservice-isolation concern — zero new using/ProjectReference; only SQL string literals inside each service's own repository changed.

plan.summary: Batch 1 of the 2026-06-14 refactor audit: fix the GetInt32-on-bigint latent-crash class. PostgreSQL COUNT(*) and SUM(integer_column) return bigint (int8); reading them with Npgsql reader.GetInt32 throws InvalidCastException at runtime. 8 SQL projection sites across 7 repository files in 6 services get an explicit ::int cast so the existing GetInt32 reads are correct. Behavior-preserving (values unchanged for the realistic count/sum range), no C# logic/DTO/signature change, no migration, no Shared change.
plan.q_intent: Q: 'hepsini sırayla yap' — execute the audit refactor backlog in INDEX order. Batch 1 = highest-confidence mechanical class (GetInt32-on-bigint). Commit, do NOT deploy ('commit'te dur').
plan.interview_notes: Sites verified by reading the actual code before editing (LLM findings are not trusted blindly): (1) Backend LeadRepository.GetFunnelStatsAsync COUNT(*) col1; (2) Backend AnalyticsRepository.GetReplyAnalyticsSummaryAsync 12x SUM(int) cols 0-7,10-13 (CASE-division cols 8,9 left, GetDouble); (3) Backend AnalyticsRepository.GetIntentMetricsAsync SUM(total_count)/SUM(handoff_count) cols 1,2 (CASE cols 3,4 left, GetDouble); (4) Outbound OutboundRepository.GetCampaignRoiAsync COUNT(cv.id) col4 (SUM(value_amount) col5 left, GetDecimal); (5) Automation AutomationRepository.GetReturnDeflectionStatsAsync COUNT(*) + COUNT(*) FILTER cols 0,1 (SUM(deflection_revenue) col2 left, GetDecimal); (6) Knowledge TemplateExtractorService.ReadIntentDistributionAsync COUNT(*) col1; (7) Appointments AppointmentsRepository.GetAvailableSlotsAsync COALESCE((SELECT COUNT(*)...),0) col5; (8) Integrations IntegrationsRepository.GetReviewRecoveryStatsAsync COUNT(*) col2. These are latent (analytics/stats endpoints not exercised by the active Dent/Medipol pilot paths), which is why they have not surfaced. The repo hot-lessons already documents this exact InvalidCastException, confirming the Npgsql version throws.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every COUNT(*)/SUM(integer) projection column that is read via reader.GetInt32 across the 8 sites now carries an explicit ::int cast in the SQL string; the corresponding GetInt32 calls, accumulator variable types, and DTO int fields are UNCHANGED.
No SUM over a decimal/numeric column (SUM(cv.value_amount), SUM(deflection_revenue)) was cast to ::int — those remain read via GetDecimal. No CASE-division column (read via GetDouble) was cast.

Only SQL string literals changed: zero changes to C# control flow, method signatures, DTO shapes, reader call types, using directives, csproj ProjectReferences. No migration, no Invekto.Shared change.
Full-solution build PASS (0 errors). dotnet build InvektoServis.sln succeeded (0 Error(s), 44 Warning(s) pre-existing).

The cast syntax is valid PostgreSQL for each shape: COUNT(*)::int, SUM(col)::int, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ...)::int (cast binds to the full aggregate-with-filter), COUNT(cv.id)::int, and COALESCE((SELECT COUNT(*) ...), 0)::int (cast binds to the COALESCE result).

verification_questions.question: Does each ::int cast preserve the exact value the GetInt32 reader already expected — i.e. for the realistic per-tenant row/sum range (leads, review_alerts, appointments-per-slot, wa_intents-per-analysis, return_deflections, daily_metrics integer sums all << int.MaxValue) the narrowing bigint->int is lossless, and is the cast syntactically valid Postgres for COUNT(*)::int, SUM(col)::int, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE ...)::int, COUNT(cv.id)::int, and COALESCE((SELECT COUNT(*)...),0)::int?

Are the changes strictly SQL-string casts with ZERO C# logic/DTO/signature/reader-type changes, and was NO decimal/numeric SUM column (SUM(cv.value_amount), SUM(deflection_revenue) — read via GetDecimal) and NO CASE-division column (read via GetDouble) erroneously cast to ::int?

Is the change free of microservice-isolation and contract impact (no new using/ProjectReference, no Invekto.Shared edit, no migration), so the 6-service single commit introduces no cross-service coupling and each repository's own SQL is the only thing touched?

Does this projection-only ::int cast leave EVERY tenant-isolation predicate byte-identical (no WHERE/JOIN/tenant_id added/removed/moved), and is the Appointments current_bookings subquery correlated-safe to the tenant-scoped outer (appointment_slots s WHERE s.tenant_id=@tid; subquery anchored to s.id) so no cross-tenant count is possible? The wa_intents analysis_id-scoped read is a PRE-EXISTING pattern (shared by sibling ReadFaqClustersAsync) unchanged by this diff; tenant_id defense-in-depth filter is a tracked separate hardening batch (see arch/codex-context.md).

Is the change purely a SQL string-literal edit with NO connection/command lifecycle change (same OpenConnectionAsync / NpgsqlCommand / ExecuteReaderAsync / await-using disposal), no new resource acquisition, no new async boundary, and no reader-ordinal shift (result shape and column order identical)?

error_handling.silent_failure_explanation: This batch removes a latent hard failure (InvalidCastException) rather than adding error handling. The affected methods previously threw at the GetInt32 read on the COUNT/SUM column; after the ::int cast they return the same int the callers already expected. No new catch/throw is introduced; existing error handling in the callers is unchanged.
